variants.title: Global users, single origin
variants.context: Users in Tokyo and New York hit the same app and static assets travel from one origin region.
variants.constraint: Large assets cross an ocean each time and latency climbs.
variants.question: What pattern reduces the latency?
variants.expectedPattern: Serve static assets and media from a CDN close to users.

variants.title: Images consume most of the time
variants.context: Images and scripts dominate page load time for an international audience.
variants.constraint: The page is dynamic but the heavy assets are static.
variants.question: What should be optimized first?
variants.expectedPattern: Deliver static media from edge caches, not the origin.
wrongChoices: Keep all assets on the origin

variants.title: Recent deploy does not appear instantly
variants.context: Users still fetch old static files even after a JS asset is updated.
variants.constraint: Old CDN copies are still cached.
variants.question: What prevents stale assets on deploy?
variants.expectedPattern: Version the asset URL with a hash so the cache sees a new file and fetches it fresh.

variants.title: Game patch day
variants.context: A new game patch is downloaded worldwide and the origin becomes a bottleneck.
variants.constraint: Large artifacts are static and global, but the origin is one region.
variants.question: What is the correct delivery model?
variants.expectedPattern: Use CDN edge distribution for the patch files.
wrongChoices: Route every user to the origin

variants.title: Slow page due to cross-continental static assets
variants.context: A marketing page contains heavy images and CSS served from a single region.
variants.constraint: The dynamic application is fine, but asset delivery is slow.
variants.question: What should be moved closer to users?
variants.expectedPattern: Static media and JS/CSS into edge cache locations.
wrongChoices: Route every request to the same app

variants.title: Origin not handling burst load
variants.context: A product launch causes huge bursts of static asset requests and the origin service is saturated.
variants.constraint: Static content is failing under popular demand.
variants.question: What absorbs the pressure?
variants.expectedPattern: A CDN edge layer that caches and serves static content near the user.

variants.title: Users in Africa wait 500ms for images
variants.context: The app is in Europe and all images are served from a single origin region.
variants.constraint: The bottleneck is physical distance, not compute.
variants.question: How do you reduce the latency?
variants.expectedPattern: Use edge caches in multiple regions and serve local copies of static assets.

variants.title: Slow JS bundle in each market
variants.context: The application sends the same large JS bundle to all users across several regions.
variants.constraint: Each region fetches the same static resource from a distant origin.
variants.question: What is the right optimization?
variants.expectedPattern: Serve the bundle from a nearby CDN edge.
wrongChoices: Move the bundle into the database

variants.title: Back-to-back deployments leave stale edge copies
variants.context: A front-end app is updated every day, but some users receive old CSS files from the edge.
variants.constraint: The CDN keeps caches until they expire.
variants.question: What pattern avoids stale content confusion?
variants.expectedPattern: Versioned asset names with a content hash.

variants.title: Heavy media library
variants.context: A learning platform serves thousands of video thumbnails globally and the origin is overloaded.
variants.constraint: The heavy files are static and heavily reused.
variants.question: What system design fits best?
variants.expectedPattern: Edge caching for thumbnails and media with cache invalidation on content updates.
wrongChoices: Direct data access from the primary DB
